artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
The Small Hours, released in 2016 on Acid Jazz Records, is Matt Berry’s seventh studio album and marks a significant point in his musical evolution. The album blends elements of rock, funk, soul, and pop, characterized by lush arrangements, smooth grooves, and Berry’s distinctive baritone vocals. Drawing inspiration from the quiet, introspective hours before dawn, the record features a warm, psychedelic-tinged sound that balances melodic sophistication with a laid-back, nocturnal atmosphere.

Within Berry’s discography, The Small Hours stands out as one of his first major releases on Acid Jazz, a label known for its focus on soulful and genre-blending music. It follows earlier works that leaned more toward experimental and folk-rock styles, showcasing a refined, accessible approach that highlights Berry’s versatility as a musician. The album received positive critical attention for its cohesive mood and polished production, with reviewers praising its blend of vintage influences and contemporary songwriting. While not a mainstream commercial breakthrough, The Small Hours solidified Berry’s reputation as a serious artist beyond his comedic persona, earning appreciation among fans of psychedelic pop and soul-inflected rock.
